answer_sentences.text: No, based on the cited RBI/UCB rules, a 2% foreclosure charge on a fixed-rate term loan to a private limited company does not appear to conflict with the pre-payment restrictions shown here.
answer_sentences.quote: In case of existing floating rate term loans sanctioned before December 31, 2025 for purposes other than business to individual borrowers with or without co- obligant(s), a UCB shall not charge pre-payment charges.

answer_sentences.text: That is because the cited no-charge rule is limited to existing floating-rate term loans, and the other quoted restriction applies only to loans up to ₹50 lakh for Tier 3 UCBs.
answer_sentences.quote: A Tier 3 UCB shall not levy any pre-payment charges on loans with sanctioned amount / limit up to ₹50 lakh.

answer_sentences.text: The policy source also shows that a 2% foreclosure charge may be levied on term loans, which is consistent with the idea that such charges can exist unless a specific RBI prohibition applies.
answer_sentences.quote: Foreclosure charges of 2% plus GST on the principal outstanding shall be levied on all term loans pre-closed by the borrower.
